observation_details:
A Mass TBT has been conducted with the museum Construction team and discuss the following important  Topic.
Excavation
Excavation is the systematic process of removing earth, rock, or other materials from the ground using tools, machinery, backhoe loader.Billder etc 
1- Never access an excavation unless a permit, 
2- protective system, and daily safety inspection are in place. 
3- Don't access an excavation deeper than 4 feet (1.2m) unless The work is authorized by a valid permt available at the excavation. 
4- A current excavation safety report, by a competent person, has been completed and made available at the excavation. 
5- Ground movement is controlled, and collapse is prevented by a protective system (sloping benching shoring, or shield) as stated in the excavation permit.. 
6- Overhead and underground services and hazards, including pipelines and electric cables, have been identified, located, and where necessary, removed, or isolated, 
7- Unauthorized entry is prevented by barricades 
8- A stairway, ladder, ramp, or other safe means of egress is available within 25 feet (7.6m)  travel in trench excavations.

A Mass TBT has been conducted with the museum Construction team and discuss the following  important Topic.
Heat Stress:
Heat Stress occurs when your Body absorb or generates more heat than it can release,Due to high temperature and hot weather conditions, all workers are advised to take proper precautions against heat stress during work activities. Heat stress can cause dehydration, dizziness, fatigue, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke which may lead to serious health hazards.
Safety Precautions:
1- Drink plenty of  water regularly.
2- Take rest breaks in shaded or cool areas.
3- Wear proper PPE and light breathable clothing.
4- Avoid direct sunlight whenever possible.
5- Report immediately if feeling dizzy, weak, or unwell.
6- Supervisors & Furman  must monitor workers continuously during hot weather activities.
7- All workers are instructed to follow heat stress safety measures to maintain a safe and healthy working environmen

A coordination meeting was conducted with the Testing & Commissioning (T&C) team with both MBL and First Fix HSE team at the museum basement regarding the implementation and control of Lock Out Tag Out (LOTO) Permit to Work (PTW) procedures.
During the meeting, the following points were discussed and agreed upon:
1-A separate LOTO PTW will be prepared for the Basement RUM and MDB rooms prior to energization activities.
2- If the Electrical Construction Team requires energization for any specific level, a separate LOTO PTW shall be prepared for that particular level before starting the activity with all required procedure including loto & standby man (security)
3- Alternatively, the T&C Team may use the same Basement LOTO PTW,from basement to all levels & the concerned Safety Officer of the respective level signs and approves the PTW before energizing the SMDB.
All teams were instructed to strictly follow the approved LOTO procedures to ensure safe energization and avoid any electrical hazards.

Fire Extinguisher use was conducted.

Workers were informed about the importance of fire extinguishers and their correct use during an emergency. They were instructed to remain calm, assess the type of fire, and ensure it is safe to use a fire extinguisher before attempting to extinguish the fire.

*The PASS method was explained as follows:*
* P – Pull the safety pin to unlock the extinguisher.
* A – Aim the nozzle at the base of the fire, not at the flames.
* S – Squeeze the handle slowly and firmly to release the extinguishing agent.
* S – Sweep the nozzle from side to side until the fire is completely extinguished.

*Workers were also reminded to:*
* Keep a safe distance from the fire while operating the extinguisher.
* Always maintain a clear escape route behind them.
* Report any discharged or damaged fire extinguisher immediately.

Mass Toolbox Talk A Mass TBT was conducted with the National theater Construction Team. The following safety points regarding Lifting Operations were discussed:

1. *Ensure a valid lift plan is available and understood by all personnel involved.*

2. *All lifting equipment must be inspected, certified, and fit for the intended task.*

3. *Verify that the load is properly secured, balanced, and stable before lifting.*

4. *Establish exclusion zones and prevent unauthorized access to the lifting area.*

5. *Only trained, competent, and authorized personnel shall perform lifting activities.*

6. *Conduct a pre-lift briefing to discuss hazards and control measures.*

7. *Maintain clear communication between the crane operator, rigger, and signalman.*

8. *Never stand, walk, or work under a suspended load.*

9. *Stop lifting operations immediately if unsafe conditions are observed.*

10. *Ensure weather conditions are suitable and safe before commencing lifting operation.*

*Topic:Lifting Operations During Summer Weather:*

1- Never perform or allow a lifting operation unless it is planned, properly supervised, and all safety controls are in place.

2- Do not perform or allow lifting operations unless:
A valid lift plan is in place, communicated, and understood by everyone involved.

3- Lifting equipment is inspected, certified, and fit for purpose.

5- Exclusion zones are established and kept clear.

6- Qualified and authorized personnel are assigned (e.g., competent rigger and operator along with a valid TUV,signal person, crane operator).

7- You stay clear of suspended loads.

8- Weather conditions are safe for lifting.

9- Adequate drinking water, shaded rest areas, and heat stress control measures must be provided for all workers.

observation_details:
A Mass TBT was conducted with the National Theatre construction team to reinforce the following Life Saving Rules:

1. *Working at Height:* Use only inspected green-tagged scaffolding with complete guardrails mid-rails toe boards and platforms. Wear a full body harness with 100% tie-off.
2. *Dropped Objects:* Do not overload scaffolds Secure all tools and materials to prevent falling object hazards.
3. *Confined Space:* No entry without a valid PTW gas testing ventilation, trained standby man proper lighting, communication and emergency equipment.
4. *Energy Isolation (LOTO):* Ensure all energy sources are isolated before work to prevent electrical shock and other hazards. Use proper PPE.
5. *Barricades & Signage:* Install barricades and warning signs around excavations confined spaces, and hazardous work areas.
6. *Excavation:* Work only with an approved excavation PTW. Provide safe access sloping/shoring an emergency plan and an exclusion zone.
7. *Lifting Operations:* Follow the lifting plan and PTW. Inspect lifting equipment and allow only authorized operators and certified riggers to perform lifting activities.
8. *Safety Compliance:* Never bypass safety rules. Follow all required safety procedures and precautions.
9. *Permit to Work (PTW):* No work shall begin without a valid PTW where required.
10. *Moving Equipment:* Stay clear of moving equipment maintain an exclusion zone use a trained banksman/watchman, and conduct a TBT before starting the activity.

Mass Toolbox Talk (TBT) was conducted for the National Theater Construction Team. The session focused on the importance of Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures to prevent accidental energization of electrical and mechanical equipment during maintenance, testing, or repair activities.

* Explained the importance of the Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) system in protecting workers from hazardous energy.
* Emphasized that no work shall be carried out on energized equipment without an approved LOTO and a valid Permit to Work (PTW).
* Instructed Electric Team to ensure that all energy sources are properly isolated, locked, and tagged before starting any work.
* Reinforced that only authorized personnel are permitted to apply or remove LOTO devices.
* Instructed all workers that energized electrical panels must remain locked at all times. Panels shall only be opened during authorized work activities and must be locked immediately after the work is completed. Under no circumstances shall any energized panel be left unlocked.

A Mass TBT has been delivered to  the Plot A Construction team and discuss the following important important Topic.
*1*: *Scaffolding Safety:*
To ensure all personnel understand the hazards associated with scaffold erection and dismantling, and to emphasize that only trained, certified, and competent scaffolders are authorized to perform this work.
*Main Hazards:*
1- Falls from height.
2- Falling tools or scaffold materials.
3- Scaffold collapse due to improper assembly.
4- Unstable or uneven foundations.
5- Overloading scaffold platforms.
6- Removal of braces or ties causing instability.
7- Slips, trips, and manual handling injuries
*2*: *LOTO* *(Lockout/Tagout)*
 *LOTO* Is a safety procedure used to isolate energy sources before maintenance or repair work to prevent accidental energization."
1-  importance of the Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) system to prevent accidental energization of electrical and mechanical equipment during maintenance or testing activities.
2- All workers were instructed to:
Never work on energized equipment without an approved LOTO and PTW.
3- Ensure all energy sources are isolated, locked, and tagged before starting work.
4- Only authorized personnel are permitted to apply or remove LOTO devices.
5- Verify zero energy before beginning any work.
6- Report any damaged or missing locks/tags immediately.

A Toolbox Talk (TBT) was conducted for the National Theater Construction Team on Scaffolding Safety. The importance of safe scaffold erection use inspection and dismantling. Workers were reminded that only trained certified and competent scaffolders are authorized to erect modify or dismantle scaffolding.

* Follow all approved scaffolding procedures at all times.
* Ensure all scaffolds are inspected before use and properly tagged.
* Maintain stable and level foundations for all scaffolds.
* Never remove braces, ties, guardrails, or other structural components without authorization.
* Use appropriate fall protection while working at height.
* Keep scaffold platforms free from debris tools and trip hazards.
* ⁠All work at height activities are currently suspended until further notice. No work at height shall be carried out unless official authorization is issued.

A Mass TBT has been delivered to  the museum Construction team and discuss the following important Topic.

*Manual Handling*
Any activity that requires  to use physical body force to lift, lower, push, pull, carry, hold, or restrain a load
*Common Hazards*
1-Lifting loads that are too heavy can lead to  Muscle and joint injuries.
2- Carrying materials over long distances may also lead to injury.
3- Slips and trips while carrying materials
5- Pinch and crush injuries to fingers and hands
6- Hands placed under suspended or moving loads.
7- Dropping materials due to poor grip or loss of balance may also lead to Hand and foot injuries.
*Control Measures*
1-Plan the lift-Check the weight, route, and destination.
2- Lift correctly - Bend your knees, keep your back straight, and hold the load close to your body.
3- Avoid twisting - Turn with your feet.
4- Know your limits - Ask for help or perform a team lift if the load is too heavy or awkward.
5- Use mechanical aids - Use trolleys, hoists, forklifts, or cranes whenever possible.

Mass Toolbox Talk (TBT) was conducted for the National Theater Construction Team on Manual Handling. The purpose of the session was to raise awareness of safe manual handling techniques and prevent injuries while lifting carrying pushing pulling or moving materials.

Key Discussion Points:

* Plan every lift by checking the weight, size lifting route, and final destination before handling any load.
* Use the correct lifting technique by bending your knees, keeping your back straight, and holding the load close to your body.
* Avoid twisting your back while carrying materials; always turn using your feet.
* Never attempt to lift loads beyond your physical capability. Request assistance or perform a team lift for heavy or awkward loads.
* Use mechanical lifting aids such as trolleys, hoists, forklifts, or cranes whenever available.
* Keep hands and fingers away from pinch points and never place them under suspended or moving loads.
* Maintain good housekeeping to prevent slips and trips while transporting materials.
* Wear appropriate PPE, including safety gloves, and communicate clearly with co-workers during manual handling activities.

HSE Lesson Learned:
Following safe manual handling practices significantly reduces the risk of back injuries, muscle strains, pinch point injuries, and other musculoskeletal disorders, helping to maintain a safe and healthy workplace.

observation_details:
A Toolbox Talk was conducted regarding Working at Height (WAH), Scaffolding, and Mobile Work Platform (MWP) Safety to reinforce safe work practices and prevent falls from height.

Key Safety Points Discussed:

* All work at height shall be properly planned, carried out under a valid Permit to Work (PTW).
* A safe working platform shall be provided. Working from ladders is only permitted for short-duration, low-risk tasks where appropriate.
* Workers shall wear a Full Body Harness (FBH) connected to a suitable anchorage or fall arrest system whenever there is a risk of falling.
* Before starting work, inspect the work area, access routes, and all fall protection equipment. Defective equipment shall not be used.
* Barricade the area below and display warning signage to protect personnel from falling objects.
* Never work at height during unsafe weather conditions or without proper supervision and authorization.
* Mobile scaffolds shall be erected, inspected, and used only by trained and authorized personnel. Platforms shall be fully decked with guardrails, mid-rails, toe boards, and locked castor wheels.
* All MWPs shall have a valid third-party inspection certificate, and operators shall hold valid competency certification. Daily pre-use inspections shall be completed before operation.

HSE Lesson Learned: Falls from height remain one of the leading causes of serious injuries and fatalities. Always ensure safe access, proper fall protection, competent supervision, and full compliance with WAH procedures before starting any work at height.

observation_details:
A comprehensive Toolbox Talk (TBT) was conducted on Manual Handling workers were reminded that every manual handling task should be assessed before starting. If a load is too heavy, bulky, unstable, or difficult to handle safely, mechanical lifting equipment or assistance from another worker must be used.
* Assess the weight and stability of the load before lifting.
* Plan the lifting route and ensure it is free from obstacles.
* Stand close to the load with feet shoulder-width apart.
* Bend the knees while keeping the back straight.
* Maintain a firm grip on the load.
* Lift smoothly using the strength of the legs, not the back.
* Keep the load close to the body throughout the movement.
* Wear the required PPE at all times, such as safety shoes, gloves, and helmets.

Mass TBT has been delivered to  the National Theater Construction team and discuss the following important Topic.

1. *LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) & Energized* Panels
    * No work is allowed near energized electrical panels without a valid LOTO Permit.
    * Even if another activity is being carried out in the same area, a LOTO Permit is mandatory for work around energized equipment.
    * A dedicated security must be present at the entrance of the energized area.
    * All personnel entering the area must sign the entry register.
    * Unauthorized persons are strictly prohibited from entering energized panel areas.
1. *Mobile Scaffolding*
    * Mobile scaffolds up to 2 meters must be fitted with 2 outriggers.
    * Mobile scaffolds above 2 meters must be fitted with 4 outriggers.
    * Ensure wheels are locked before use.
    * Do not move the scaffold while workers are on it.
    * Inspect the scaffold before use and report any defects immediately.
1. *A-Type Ladder*
   A-Type ladder must be inspected by the Scaffolding Inspector, and a valid inspection tag must be attached before use. The ladder shall not be used without inspection and a valid tag.
    * Do not use damaged or defective ladders.
1. *Hot Work*
    * A valid Hot Work Permit is required before starting any hot work.
    * Check the welding machine and accessories before use.
    * Ensure all required PPE is worn.
    * Keep a fire extinguisher/fire blanket available at the work location.
5. *Cuplock Scaffolding*
    * Work on Cuplock Scaffolding is not allowed until further notice.
    * Do not use or access Cuplock scaffolding unless official approval is issued.

HSE Team conducted a Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) safety training to raise awareness among all workers regarding the hazards associated with energized electrical equipment and the mandatory control measures required before starting any work.

* No work is permitted near energized electrical panels without a valid and approved LOTO Permit.
* A LOTO Permit is mandatory for any activity carried out in the vicinity of energized electrical equipment, even if the work is non-electrical.
* Only authorized personnel are permitted to enter energized electrical panel areas.
* A dedicated security guard must be present at the entrance of the energized area to control access at all times.
* All personnel entering and leaving the energized area must sign the entry register.
* Energized areas must be clearly barricaded and provided with appropriate warning signs.
* Always maintain safe clearance from energized electrical equipment and follow all site safety procedures.
* Any unsafe condition, damaged barricade, or unauthorized entry must be reported immediately to the HSE Team or the responsible supervisor.
* Failure to comply with LOTO requirements may result in serious injury, fatality, or disciplinary action.

A Mass TBT has been delivered to  the museum Construction team and discuss the following important Topic.
Falling Object: 
A falling object is any tool, material, or equipment that accidentally drops from a height due to improper handling, poor storage, or inadequate securing methods. Falling objects can cause serious injuries, fatalities, or property damage at the workplace
Control Measures:
1- Always use tool lanyards when working at height to prevent tools from falling.
2- Inspect all hand tools before use and ensure they are in good condition.
3- Do not keep loose tools or materials near the edge of scaffolding or platforms.
4- Install toe boards and proper barricades below the work area.
5- Keep unauthorized persons away from the drop zone.
6 - Never throw tools or materials from height.
7- Wear proper PPE, including a safety helmet and safety shoes.
8- Maintain good housekeeping and remove unnecessary materials from the work area.
9-  Report any falling object incident or unsafe condition immediately to the supervisor.

observation_details:
An HSE campaign was conducted today at the National Theater Basement with the participation of the First Fix Company, ICAD Company, and Signal Company.

All teams were informed that no personnel or team is permitted to enter or work inside an energized room without a valid LOTO PTW. The LOTO PTW must be properly prepared and signed by all four authorized parties:

1. First Fix LOTO Engineer
2. MBL LOTO Engineer
3. First Fix HSE/Safety
4. MBL HSE/Safety

All four signatures are mandatory before entering or commencing any work inside an energized room.

It was also communicated that any company/team working inside an energized room must have dedicated security stationed at the entrance throughout the activity. A LOTO attendance sheet must be maintained, and every person entering the energized room must sign IN before entry and sign OUT after completing the work and exiting the room.

Furthermore, the responsible Engineer, Supervisor, or Foreman of any team working inside an energized room must possess a valid LOTO training certificate. Personnel without valid LOTO training certification are not authorized to enter or work inside energized rooms.

All participating teams were instructed to strictly comply with the LOTO PTW, attendance, security, and training requirements to ensure safe control of energized areas.

A Mass TBT has been delivered to  the museum Construction team and discuss the following important points.
Working at heights: working at height refers to any work that is done above ground level using scaffolding or roofs. It also includes working on ladders, elevated work platforms.
Key safety control:
1- Use proper access and a safe working platform.
2- Wear a Full Body Harness (FBH).
3- Connect the harness to a suitable lifeline/anchorage point.
4- Ensure scaffolding is inspected and properly tagged.
5- Provide guardrails and toe boards.
6- Keep the work area barricaded and free from falling-object hazards.
7- Use proper ladders and maintain three-point contact.
8- Ensure a valid PTW and risk assessment are available where required.

- Avoiding shortcuts and following approved work procedures.

* Use proper lighting when working or walking in dark areas.

A Mass TBT was conducted by the HSE Team for the National Theater Construction Team. The following important safety topics were discussed:

. Dehydration & Safe Drinking Practices
Working in a hot construction environment can cause the body to lose a significant amount of water and essential salts through sweating. If these fluids are not replaced, dehydration can develop and may affect concentration, physical performance, decision-making, and overall safety.

Key Points Discussed:

* Drink water regularly throughout the working day; do not wait until you feel thirsty.
* Take adequate rest breaks in designated shaded/cool areas.
* Avoid excessive consumption of caffeinated or energy drinks during hot work.
* ⁠Encourage co-workers to stay hydrated and report any signs of heat stress.

MASS TOOLBOX TALK

Topic: Never Work Alone
Conducted by: HSE Team
Date: 06-09-2026
Location: National Theater

A Mass Toolbox Talk (TBT) was conducted by the HSE Team for the National Theater Construction Team. The session focused on the importance of the Never Work Alone principle and the Buddy System, particularly when carrying out high-risk activities.

Key Safety Points Discussed
1. Never Work Alone
    Never work alone during high-risk activities. Ensure a responsible person is available to monitor, assist, and raise the alarm in an emergency.
2. Buddy System
    Work in pairs or teams. Your buddy helps identify hazards, provides assistance, and responds during emergencies.
3. High-Risk Activities
    Maintain proper communication and supervision when working at height, in confined spaces, near energized equipment, during lifting, or other high-risk work.
4. Emergency Response
    Know how to raise the alarm and who to contact. Never put yourself at additional risk to help others.
5. Stop Work Authority
    Every worker has the right and responsibility to STOP WORK if an unsafe condition or missing safety control is identified.

observation_details:
This week’s Mass Tool Box Talk session was conducted at KSP Project – National Theatre. The discussion was mainly focused on strengthening PTW compliance, ensuring proper PPE usage discipline, and maintaining daily housekeeping and material arrangements to prevent unsafe conditions at site. PTW topic was specially stressed – incomplete PTW, unsigned PTW, and PTW filled by unauthorized persons will not be accepted.

Key Points Discussed:
•	PTW must be complete, correct and properly signed before starting any task.
•	Only authorized persons are allowed to fill PTW – workers are not allowed to fill PTW.
•	Supervisor MUST review PTW before initiating work.
•	PPE Violation is strictly prohibited – anyone found without PPE will face disciplinary action.
•	Daily housekeeping and proper material arrangement must be maintained at all work areas.

* 📋 Weekly Mass TBT *

Date: 23-11-2025
Location: National Theater – KSP Project
Conducted by: HSE Supervisor Waqar
Participants: All Site Workers & Supervisors

TBT Topics Covered
1. Work at Height Safety
•	All personnel working above 2 meters must use a full body harness, properly anchored to a certified anchorage point.
•	Only approved and safe platforms scaffolds, ladders, or mobile platforms are allowed for work at height.
•	Ensure scaffolding is inspected and tagged Green  Safe Red  Unsafe before use.

2. Permit to Work
•	Supervisors must ensure the PTW is properly filled, approved, and understood by the work team before beginning any task.
* ⁠Follow all precautions and control measures mentioned in the permit.

3. Hot Work Safety
•	Hot work (welding, cutting, grinding) must only start after obtaining a Hot Work Permit.
•	Workers must use proper PPE For Hot Work activity.
•	Ensure fire extinguishers are available, and the work area is free from flammable materials.

observation_details:
Making holes in a safety helmet makes it unsafe and not acceptable.

What happens when holes are made in a helmet:

The helmet becomes weak.
There is a high risk of head injury even from small falling objects.
Electrical risk increases because the insulation is damaged.
It is a site safety violation.

Important:
Drilling, punching, or making holes in a helmet is strictly not allowed.
If ventilation is needed, only manufacturer-approved ventilated helmets should be used.

Conclusion:
A helmet with holes is unsafe and must be replaced immediately.
close_out_details: Confiscated.

close_out_details: Refresher training was conducted on work-at-height PPE and ESSOW requirements. A proper podium ladder was provided for safe access. A verbal warning was issued to the team, and the activity was allowed to resume under compliance.

observation_details: It has observed that a hot work activity was carrying out at undesignated area.
close_out_details: The activity was suspended, and the worker was shifted to the designated area.

observation_details: Observed the plumbing team carrying out work activities in an area with poor illumination, which poses the risk of slips, trips, falls, incorrect installation, and potential injury to personnel.
close_out_details: Temporary lighting was installed visibility was adequte.

observation_details: Observed the plumbing team performing their activities while some plumbers were not wearing hard hats, which could lead to head injuries from falling objects.
close_out_details: Workers were instructed to wear hard hats immediately. The supervisor conducted a site briefing on mandatory PPE requirements and ensured compliance.

observation_details: Observed the plumbing team using an uninspected ladder with damaged rubber feet, which could lead to lad  der instability, slipping, and potential fall injuries to personnel.
close_out_details: The ladder was immediately removed from service and tagged as unsafe and the supervisor instructed to provide safe and nspected ladder for the activity.

observation_details: Found the electrical team involved in concrete chipping activities while a worker was not wearing eye protection, which could lead to eye injuries from flying debris and dust.
close_out_details: Work was stopped immediately and suitable eye protection was provided and brief tool box talk conducted to the team for importance of PPE.

observation_details: Found a dyna driver operating the vehicle without wearing seat belt, which could lead to serious injury in case of sudden braking or an accident.
close_out_details: The driver was instructed to stop the vehicle and instructed to wear seat belt.

observation_details: Guardrails were not installed on the mobile scaffold during work at height by the electrical subcontractor. Zone 5c
close_out_details: Work was stopped immediately, and the mobile scaffold was made compliant by installing full guardrails before resuming activities.

observation_details: A fire extinguisher was found without nozzle hose at zone 5.
close_out_details: Replaced the fire extinguisher on the scissor lift safety compliance verified.

observation_details: Painting work on the duct was being performed without wearing a coverall suit; the activity was suspended until proper PPE was worn at FEC
close_out_details: The painting activity resumed only after the required coverall suit and appropriate PPE were worn at FEC.

observation_details: Welding /cutting sparks flew outward from the work area during the activity, extending beyond the work zone. Zone 4
close_out_details: The welding/cutting activity was stopped immediately. The work area was properly covered with fire blanked.

observation_details: The worker was observed to work without the required PPE (safety gloves). FEC zone 1
close_out_details: The worker has been provided with proper safety gloves and instructed to wear full PPE while working at site.

observation_details: Poor cable management was observed, with electric cables routed through metallic pipes.
close_out_details: The issue has been rectified, and proper cable management has been implemented. Electrical cables were rerouted using illuminated poles in accordance with safety standards.

observation_details: Observed that Subcon MSSCO personnel were using a scissor lift very close to other subcon (TKE) material storage at Ground Floor, poses the risk of materials damage in addition to approaching restricted work zone.
close_out_details: Activity suspended and the responsible supervisor and crew instructed to ensure adequate space and clearance in addition to adequate barricade and signs to prevent collision and falling objects.

observation_details: Observed that during work at height, the safety harness lanyard was not connected, posing a fall hazard. Zone 5c
close_out_details: Work at height stopped immediately. The safety harness lanyard was properly connected and verified.

observation_details: Material accumulation on the scissor lift working platform poses the risk of slips, trips, and falls.
close_out_details: The operative instructed to clean the platform immediately to ensure good housekeeping compliance over the platform.
